audit.why: 48.58% over 1659 games and the chart [Sion, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia, Skill, Sion] already agrees row for row between the packet and win[]; the mirrored lillia__sion audit reports the same and moved no tokens. No chart edits.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike treats her ultimate as an unconditional answer to your engage, and no cooldown is attached to it.
audit.why: Lilting Lullaby only makes enemies drowsy if they already have Dream Dust on them from her passive — it is not a point-and-click sleep on a clean target. It is also 150s at rank 1, which makes 'threaten it and then use R elsewhere' a very long window rather than a vague one.
audit.corrected: The Dream Dust precondition and the 150s cooldown written into whys[4], mid and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: late claims her damage is 'a percentage-flat AP DoT rather than true-damage scaling' and that 'Blooming Blows does not multiply with your HP... so bulk actually wins here'. spikes[3] and whys[6] repeat it.
audit.why: Both halves are backwards. Dream-Laden Bough (P) deals 'additional max Health damage over time' — it scales directly with the HP Sion stacks. And Blooming Blows deals 'extra true damage on the edge', which is exactly the true-damage scaling the page says she lacks. The brief flags this as resistances-invalidated: raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here.
audit.corrected: Passive stated as max-health damage over time, Q's outer edge stated as true damage, and the itemisation conclusion corrected — health and Heartsteel stacks hold up, resistances do not.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere for the abilities the page tells you to play around.
audit.why: Blooming Blows is 6s at rank 1 down to 4s at rank 5 — that is why the orbit never stops. Swirlseed is a flat 12s at every rank, so a whiffed seed is a countable window to step up.
audit.corrected: Both written into whys[3] and mid.

edits.before: She loops Blooming Blows continuously through levels 4 and 5, and her Swirlseed (E) slow keeps you in her DoT field — you cannot reliably charge Q without being dodged.
edits.after: She loops Blooming Blows every 4-5 seconds and its outer edge adds true damage, while Swirlseed's flat 12s slow holds you inside it — you cannot charge Q without being dodged.

edits.before: Her R (Lilting Lullaby) puts you to sleep mid all-in and her team punishes the wasted Unstoppable Onslaught — use your ult for map pressure, not solo dives into her range.
edits.after: Lilting Lullaby only makes you drowsy if her passive Dream Dust is already on you — arrive unpoked and her 150s ult has nothing to land on, so spend yours on map pressure.

edits.before: Your Heartsteel compound HP makes her flat-AP DoT lose effectiveness ratio-wise; your W-shield value scales with max HP and your zombie passive threatens her even through death.
edits.after: Her passive burns a share of your max health and her Q edge is true damage, so buy health over resistances; your W-shield and the zombie passive are what actually beat her.

edits.before: Your max-HP total dwarfs her DoT output at full build — Heartsteel compound interest and your W-shield value make you nearly unkillable in a sustained brawl she cannot disengage from with R sleep.
edits.after: Her passive burns max health and the edge of Blooming Blows is true damage, so armour and MR do nothing — win instead with Heartsteel bulk, W-shield cycles and the zombie passive in brawls she cannot kite out of.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are Lillia's control window — her Blooming Blows stacks are maxed, her E slow (Swirlseed) sets up repeated poke, and at 6 her R sleep ends any all-in you force into her. Use your E (Roar of the Slayer) armor shred only when she over-steps into your range; do not blow it chasing an accelerating target. At level 6 your Unstoppable Onslaught (R) can close her gap on paper, but she will R-sleep you mid-charge if she reads the angle — threaten the ult to make her respect it, then use it for map transit or objective engages with your jungler rather than solo all-ins she can simply sleep through.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 are Lillia's control window — Blooming Blows cycles every 4-5 seconds, her Swirlseed (E) is a flat 12s slow that sets up repeated poke, and at 6 her R threatens any all-in. Use your E (Roar of the Slayer) armor shred only when she over-steps into your range; do not blow it chasing an accelerating target. At level 6 your Unstoppable Onslaught (R) can close her gap on paper, but Lilting Lullaby only reaches targets already carrying her Dream Dust — step in unpoked and it cannot touch you. Threaten the ult, then spend it on transit or objective engages with your jungler.

edits.before: At 2+ items your max-HP pool becomes genuinely punishing for a champion whose damage is a percentage-flat AP DoT rather than true-damage scaling — Lillia's Blooming Blows does not multiply with your HP the way Vayne W or Gwen scissors do, so bulk actually wins here. Force brawls in tight corridors like Baron or Dragon pit where her kite range collapses; your zombie passive (Glory in Death) after a late-game death still threatens her and her teammates for several seconds. If she is ahead, do not chase through open terrain — group with your team and use your R to initiate teamfights where her sleep hits the whole backline rather than just you.
edits.after: At 2+ items you are a frontline she struggles to kill outright, but know what her damage actually is: Dream-Laden Bough burns a share of your MAX health over time and the outer edge of Blooming Blows is true damage, so armour and magic resist are the wrong buys — raw health and Heartsteel stacks are what hold up. Force brawls in tight corridors like Baron or Dragon pit where her kite range collapses; your zombie passive (Glory in Death) after a late death still threatens her team for several seconds. Lilting Lullaby needs Dream Dust on its target, so arriving unpoked blanks her 150s ult. If she is ahead, do not chase through open terrain — group and start fights with your R.

notes: The late-game section gave the player an itemisation conclusion that is the exact inverse of the kit: it said her damage does not scale with HP and is not true damage, and therefore bulk wins. Riot's text says her passive deals additional MAX HEALTH damage over time and her Q deals extra TRUE damage on the outer edge — so resistances are the wasted stat, which is what the brief's resistances-invalidated flag is pointing at. Health is still correct to buy (it is Sion's whole kit), but for the shield and the brawl, not because it blunts her. Second real fix: Lilting Lullaby is conditional on Dream Dust, so 'she just sleeps you mid-charge' overstates it.
